info.title: kestrel link
info.summary: The connection between an Instance and the control plane.
info.description: The supervisor inside an Instance opens this connection outward: server-sent events down, POST up, plain HTTP with no protocol upgrade. A supervisor lives with its Instance, not its Session: it authenticates as the Instance, and every Session on the Instance is begun, prompted and stopped over the one link.

post.summary: Answer a read the stream asked of this Instance.
post.description: The body is streamed and piped to the operator who asked. A read nobody has begun answering 10 s after it was sent is given up on, and its answer is then refused. A JSON answer is one `Answer`; bytes are a file's contents as they are.

204.description: The answer was taken, or the operator stopped reading it.

get.summary: Take what a Session's Harness is spawned with.
get.description: Answered as the supervisor spawns a Session's Harness, and asked at no other moment: the control plane decrypts them here. Every Provider Credential the Session's Organization holds, and the variables and files of the Subscription Profile its Workspace names, which no other Workspace's Session is handed. Variables reach that process's environment and nothing else; files are written beneath the agent's home for the length of the Session. Only a Session the Instance is carrying is answered for, so an Instance between Sessions is handed nothing.

200.description: The variables and files the Harness is spawned with.

patch.summary: Hand back the files the Harness rewrote.
patch.description: A harness refreshes its login where it keeps it, and a refresh may revoke the login it replaced, so the supervisor hands back every file it was given that changed before it reports the Session's turn over. Only files the Workspace's Subscription Profile already holds are taken; any other path is ignored.

204.description: What the profile holds is what was handed back.

get.summary: Read one window of the Transcript of the Workspace holding this Instance.
get.description: At most one window of entries, in order, and the cursor the next read resumes from. A cursor names a position rather than a read held open, so it still walks after the control plane restarts; one that names no position in this Transcript is refused rather than silently restarting the walk.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The cursor a previous read ended with. Absent means from the beginning.

parameters.name: window
parameters.description: How many entries to return at most.

parameters.name: kinds
parameters.description: Comma-separated Transcript kinds. The cursor advances across every examined seq, including omitted kinds.

parameters.name: summaries
parameters.description: Summarize omitted narration and detail, across every shared-state boundary even when shared state is not selected. With every kind selected there are no summaries.

parameters.name: first_seq
parameters.description: Inclusive first seq of an Activity expansion. Select every kind to read its entries.

parameters.name: last_seq
parameters.description: Inclusive last seq of an Activity expansion; must be at least first_seq. The finite range ends when caught up.

200.description: One window of the Transcript, and the cursor the next read resumes from.

get.summary: Hold open the stream of instructions for an Instance.
get.description: One stream per Instance, carrying every Session's instructions in order, each naming its Session: a Session's `start` always follows the last Session's `stop`. Replays every instruction after `Last-Event-ID`, then stays open. The stream closes when the Instance is let go.

parameters.name: Last-Event-ID
parameters.description: The seq of the last instruction this supervisor received. Absent means from the beginning.

200.description: The stream is open. Each event carries an instruction and the Session it is for as its data, the instruction's kind as its event name, and its seq as its id. An event named `read` carries a `Read` instead, and no id: it is never stored, and a reconnect never replays it.

post.summary: Report something about an Instance, or the Session it carries, to the control plane.
post.description: Delivery is at-least-once: a supervisor that loses the answer to a report sends it again under the same seq, and the control plane takes it once. Seqs are counted within the Session a report names; one that skips a report the Session has yet to make is refused. A report about a Session the Instance no longer carries — it has ended, or its lease has passed — is answered 410, and the supervisor lets that Session go.

202.description: The report was accepted. Connected reports return the Workspace checkout declaration, so a supervisor can inspect a held Instance even between Sessions.

instanceCredential.description: The credential issued for the Instance when its supervisor was started. Refused once the Instance is let go, and once another supervisor is started on it.

instance.name: instance
instance.description: The Instance this supervisor runs on, as `<driver>/<name>`, percent-encoded as one path segment.

session.name: session
session.description: The Session the Instance is carrying, which alone is handed anything of a Session's.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before asking again. Present on a 503 only when the database was busy, which asking again can clear.

Credentials.description: What a Harness is spawned with to reach a model: the Provider Credentials of the Session's Organization and the Subscription Profile its Workspace names.

variables.description: The environment variable each credential is read from, and what it is read as. A profile's variable takes the place of a Provider Credential of the same name.

files.description: Each file's path beneath the agent's home, and its contents.
Each rewritten file's path beneath the agent's home, and what it now holds.

Instruction.description: What the control plane asks of an Instance, for the Session it names.

session.description: The Session this instruction is for.

Start.description: Take up the Session: check out, then open its one agent conversation and prompt its first turn. A checkout that fails is reported as the Session finished failed, and the Session never starts.

turn.description: The seq of the Turn this prompt begins, which an interrupt names.

prompt.description: The agent's whole prompt, sent exactly as given: the Workspace's unfollowed Brief, or the message or messages that started this Session with earlier Transcript entries as labeled context ahead of them.

Unbriefed.description: Take up the Session without a Brief: check out, then open its one agent conversation and prompt nothing. The Session waits unbriefed for its first message. A checkout or spawn that fails is reported as the Session finished failed, and the Session never starts.

Prompt.description: Prompt the next turn, in the conversation the Session's first turn opened. Sent only once the turn before it is answered.

turn.description: The seq of the Turn this prompt begins, which an interrupt names.

prompt.description: The agent's whole prompt, sent exactly as given.

SetOption.description: Change one of the Session's harness options before its next prompt. Durable, so it is applied once, in order ahead of any prompt after it (ADR-0041).

option.description: The option's id as the harness reported it, or the synthesized mode's id for a harness that offers only legacy modes.

value.description: The value to set, as the harness offers it.

participant.description: The person making the change, by the participant name rule.

Read.description: A read of the Instance's checkouts, answered by POSTing to `answers/{request}`. Paths are `<repo>/<path>`, resolved through symlinks, and refused outside that repository's checkout.

ReadFiles.description: One directory level, at most 5,000 entries, each marked tracked, untracked or ignored. No path lists the repositories.

ReadFile.description: A file: UTF-8 text up to 1 MiB as a `text` answer, otherwise, or when `raw`, its bytes.

AnswerRefused.description: Outside the checkout, or not the kind of entry the read needs.

Checkout.description: What the agent works in: each repository cloned into the working directory, on the branch, which is cut from the base when the repository does not have it yet.

Harness.description: What the supervisor spawns for this Session, which may be another Agent's than the last Session's on the Instance.

auth.description: The ACP authentication method to log the agent in with, for an agent that requires one.

model.description: The model the Session named. Absent leaves the harness's default.

mode.description: The mode the Session named. Absent leaves the harness's default.

thought_level.description: The thought level the Session named. Absent leaves the harness's default.

Stop.description: End the Session's agent conversation and let the Session go. The supervisor stays on the link.

Interrupt.description: Cancel the Turn the Session is in without ending it: the conversation and the Instance stay, and a Turn held for it follows. A supervisor whose Turn in flight is not the one named does nothing, so a cancel that arrives after its Turn answered never reaches the next one.

turn.description: The seq of the Turn to cancel.

Report.description: What a supervisor tells the control plane. `connected` and `heartbeat` are about the Instance; every other report names the Session it is about, and one that belongs to its ordered account of that Session carries a seq and is taken once.

session.description: The Session this report is about. Required on every report but `connected`, `heartbeat` and `stderr`.

Ready.description: The harness is up and its agent conversation open, with no Turn started: an unbriefed Session is ready for its first message. Not numbered.

Connected.description: The supervisor is on the link, and this is what is running in the Instance.

Heartbeat.description: The supervisor is still alive, and holds out the lease of the Session it carries for another turn of the clock. Sent for as long as the Instance lives; when it stops, a Session's lease expires and the Session ends failed.

Stderr.description: Lines the Harness wrote to stderr, oldest first, sent as it writes them. They are the operator's diagnostics, never anything the agent said, and a line the link was not there to take in time is not sent again.

Model.description: Which model the Harness is on for this turn — the one the Session's Agent named, or the harness's own default when it named none. Absent for a harness that lets no client select one at all.

Said.description: A message completed at an ID change or Turn boundary; a chunk without an ID completes immediately.

UsageReport.description: What the Harness has spent so far, unnumbered and transient: held in memory beside the running tools, sent at most once a second at the window's trailing edge, and never recorded (ADR-0041).

OptionChanged.description: The harness answered a person's option change: the whole list it left, or why it refused. Numbered, because the control plane settles the pending change and writes the entry once (ADR-0041).

participant.description: The person who asked for the change.

option.description: The option's id the change named.

category.description: The category the option belongs to.

from.description: What the option was set to before the change.

to.description: What it was set to. Absent when the harness refused.

refused.description: Why the harness refused, when it did.

options.description: The harness's whole option list after a change that applied; empty when it refused.

Answered.description: The agent answered the turn, and its conversation waits for another prompt. The Session goes on, trailing until its agent's work settles. It carries what the Harness had spent when the turn ended, which is what the Session read keeps.

usage.description: What the Harness had spent when the turn ended. Absent for a supervisor that never heard a usage update.

Interrupted.description: The working turn was cancelled at kestrel's request: its open tool calls were closed and no answer follows. The conversation and the Instance stay.

trailing.description: Background tasks or subagents the agent started still run, so the Session is trailing rather than waiting until they settle.

Settled.description: The trailing Session's agent has nothing open and has been quiet for the quiet period, so the Session is waiting. Sent after the checkout observed then, which is the report the Unpublished Work hold reads. Activity after it needs no report of its own: a later unit report, or a `session_state` carrying `last_activity_at`, makes the Session trailing again.

CheckoutObserved.description: What git says of each of the Project's repositories once the agent has stopped working in it, reported before the Session finishes. The control plane judges from it whether the Instance holds work that exists nowhere else; a Session that finishes without one leaves its Instance held.

Observed.description: One repository's checkout: counted from git when it could be read, and why not when it could not.

branch.description: The branch checked out, or null on a detached HEAD.

untracked.description: Files git neither tracks nor ignores.

uncommitted.description: Tracked paths changed and not committed, staged or not.

unpushed.description: Commits on any local branch or HEAD that no remote-tracking branch reaches.

Finished.description: The Session is over, and this is how it went: its conversation failed, or it never started. The supervisor lets the Session go after saying so, and stays on the link. It carries what the Harness had spent when it ended, so a Session that ends mid-turn still records it.

usage.description: What the Harness had spent when the Session ended. Absent for a supervisor that never heard a usage update.

Seq.description: Where a report sits in the sequence the supervisor numbers for its Session. The control plane takes each number once, so a report replayed after an answer that never arrived changes the record once.

because.description: Why it failed. Absent when it succeeded.

Usage.description: Cumulative rather than per turn: the last report of it is the one that stands.

cost.description: What it has cost so far. Absent when the harness does not say.

Page.description: One bounded window of a Transcript, and where the next read resumes.

cursor.description: Where the next read resumes. Null only for a read that started at the beginning and found nothing.

more.description: Whether entries were waiting beyond this window when it was read.

Activity.description: Read-time summary of omitted narration and detail between consecutive shared-state entries. first_seq identifies the whole Activity, including selected kinds, and stays stable across pages and reconnects. last_seq is the highest Activity seq examined; its SSE id advances the global cursor. A closed replacement precedes the closing shared-state entry even when no detail was added. No summary is stored.

started_at.description: Earliest start among omitted unexpired entries.

finished_at.description: Latest finish among omitted unexpired entries.

anomaly.description: An omitted call was interrupted or unresolved.

closed.description: The next shared-state boundary has been examined. Followers replace open summaries by first_seq and CLI followers print only this final replacement.

Recorded.description: One Transcript entry, and where it sits in the order.

ExpiredEntry.description: Narration or detail expired in place after 30 days from append, including in sealed Workspaces. The enclosing record retains its original kind, seq and appended_at, with session_id null; all content, completion metadata and payload references are removed.

expired_at.description: When the sweep replaced the entry.

Entry.description: One completed unit of the Workspace Transcript.

Brief.description: The instruction a Workspace started with, rendered by the Trigger that fired or supplied by an operator.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

BriefSource.description: Who supplied a Brief: the Trigger whose firing rendered it, or an operator, under the participant name they declared if they declared one.

participant.description: The participant who joined directly before the Brief, or null when the operator declared no name and no one joined.

SessionStarted.description: A Session started on behalf of the Workspace.

Messages.description: Messages that arrived while a Session was active, drained as one Transcript entry.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

SpokenMessage.description: One Participant's message within a drained group.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

SessionEnded.description: A Session ended, and how it went.

InstanceReleased.description: A person released the Workspace's Instance, destroying it and whatever it held that was never pushed.

unpublished.description: What it held that existed nowhere else, as judged when it was released; null when it held nothing.

Work.description: Unnumbered and non-durable. Sent on connect, when a two-second check during a turn finds a change, and at turn close. Does not alter the durable checkout observation.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.
Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

status.description: The status the Harness last reported for the call.

input.description: Inline JSON, or a PayloadReference when the serialized value exceeds 65536 bytes.

result.description: Inline JSON, or a PayloadReference when the serialized value exceeds 65536 bytes.

closing_reason.description: Why kestrel closed the call at a Turn boundary; null when the Harness settled it.

payload_fields.description: Fields containing payload references; absent means every content field is inline.

RunningUnit.description: Work an adapter declared it runs apart from any tool call, such as a Claude background task, open until the adapter settles it. A settled unit adds no Transcript entry.

status.description: The status the Harness last reported for the call.

closing_reason.description: Why kestrel closed the call at a Turn boundary; null when the Harness settled it.

SessionState.description: A whole transient Session snapshot, sent on changes and reconnect: the running tools and adapter units, whether a message or thought is still buffering, what the Harness has spent, and when its agent last showed activity while trailing. Unnumbered; never enters the Transcript and never recorded.

usage.description: What the Harness has spent so far. Absent until it reports one.

last_activity_at.description: When the agent last showed activity, present only while the Session trails its answer. A waiting Session that reports it is trailing again.

SessionInfo.description: The Session's whole bookkeeping state: the harness's title for the conversation, its config options and the commands it offers (ADR-0041). Sent when any of it changes and again after a reconnect; unnumbered, because it is idempotent and the whole state goes up each time.

SessionOption.description: A harness config option, whole: what it is, what it may be and what it is now. A legacy harness that offers only `modes` is reported through a synthesized option of the `mode` category.

category.description: `mode`, `model`, `model_config`, `thought_level`, or the harness's own string, which may begin with `_`.

current.description: The current value: a value id for a select, a boolean for a toggle.

values.description: The offered values of an ungrouped select; empty for a grouped one and for a boolean.

groups.description: The offered values of a grouped select; empty for an ungrouped one.

SessionCommand.description: A command the harness offers for the Session, as a composer lists it.

PayloadReference.description: A body field exceeding 65536 bytes, fetched under its owning Workspace; message, thought and brief text use raw UTF-8, while plans, batched messages and tool input/results use compact JSON.
